A.explanation: Infra-red has longer wavelength than visible light, about $10^{-5} \text{ m}$, not 1000 times smaller.

B.explanation: Microwaves have much longer wavelength than visible light, about $10^{-2} \text{ m}$, so they are larger not smaller.

C.explanation: Ultraviolet is next to visible on the short-wavelength side but only about 10 times smaller, near $10^{-8} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: A wavelength 1000 times smaller than visible light is about $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, which lies in the X-ray region.

walkthrough: Visible light has wavelength of order $\lambda \approx 5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, in the range $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
The question asks for $1000$ times smaller, so calculate $\lambda = 5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} / 1000 \approx 5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
Recall the spectrum in order of decreasing wavelength: infra-red and microwaves are longer than visible, while ultraviolet then X-rays are shorter than visible.
Ultraviolet is only roughly a factor of $10$ shorter than visible, around $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, whereas X-rays extend down to about $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-13} \text{ m}$.
The estimated $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ falls clearly in the X-ray range. This is option D.
